name: Product Boundary and Runtime Topology

product_boundary.deployment_model: single-user local desktop installation exposing a same-machine browser UI
product_boundary.authoritative_application_boundary: one Python host process per canonical SOMA data instance
product_boundary.authoritative_datastore: SQLite through HLD-02 owned persistence interfaces
product_boundary.network_scope: supported loopback origin only; no LAN, WAN, cloud, or remote-listen mode in Beta 1.0
product_boundary.browser_role: untrusted presentation client of the local application boundary; never domain or persistence authority
product_boundary.runtime_assets: application runtime assets are local and version-matched with the installed host; no runtime CDN or internet dependency
product_boundary.lineage: Beta repository, persistence, migrations, packaging, and releases remain independent from Zeus and SOMA Alpha
product_boundary.distribution: private proprietary internal product; release and source material remain restricted to authorized internal use

responsibilities: runtime lifecycle and local control surface

non_authoritative_processes.count: zero or more windows/tabs of the supported local operator browser
non_authoritative_processes.lifecycle: may open, close, reload, or restart without becoming the SOMA application lifetime

runtime_topology.helper_process_policy: No helper process may own unique domain truth or write authoritative state independently. A later LLD may justify a bounded helper for unsafe/expensive adapter work only through the same staged/application transaction boundary.

release_exclusions: Alpha database migration as an executable starting point

delegated_design.HLD-02: SQLite connection, migration, runtime registry persistence mechanics, durable jobs, and persistence lifecycle
delegated_design.HLD-11: browser shell, routing, interaction state, responsive workbenches, and client implementation
delegated_design.HLD-13: local-run authentication/trust, encryption, backup/recovery, diagnostics security, CSRF/origin controls, and shutdown authorization
delegated_design.HLD-14: transaction, audit, temporal, history, idempotency, and derived-state cross-cutting rules
delegated_design.LLD-01: exact Python server library, port selection mechanics, launchers, tray toolkit, process supervision, API transport details, and shutdown implementation
delegated_design.LLD-12: packaging, release assembly, platform/browser matrix details, and installation artifacts
